 Bulls Routed 135-92 by Raptors in Season Opener
 The Bulls never led, turned it over 27 times and shot 4 of 36 from three in a 135-92 opening-night loss to the Raptors in Toronto.
 by Tony Marchese • 5 hours ago Feb 5, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Toronto Raptors forward Brandon Ingram (3) holds the ball from Chicago Bulls forward Patrick Williams (44) in the second half at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Chicago Bulls Facebook Tweet 
 The Tiago Splitter era started with a long night in Toronto. The Bulls never led, gave the ball away 27 times and fell 135-92 to the Raptors at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday, a 43-point loss in the season opener that was out of hand before the first quarter ended.
 Toronto scored the first seven points and kept going. Immanuel Quickley hit three threes from 25 feet or deeper in the final 4:19 of the quarter; Scottie Barnes and Ja’Kobe Walter added threes of their own, and the Raptors led 43-23 after one. It was 69-44 at the half, and the lead reached 48 in the fourth.
 Turnovers and Threes Sink Chicago
 The numbers tell the story. Chicago shot 4-for-36 from three and 32% overall. Toronto turned the Bulls’ 27 turnovers into 35 points, while the Bulls got eight points off the Raptors’ 11. The Raptors also won fast-break points 34-13 and points in the paint 58-40, and they had 31 assists to Chicago’s 16.
 The one thing that kept the score from getting worse was the free-throw line. The Bulls went 34 of 47 and grabbed 21 offensive rebounds, but that couldn’t make up for the misses and giveaways.
 A Rough Debut for Wilson
 Caleb Wilson , coming off his cleanest game of the preseason in the 133-116 win over Minnesota , had 16 points on 7-of-21 shooting with nine turnovers in 32 minutes in his first regular-season game. He was minus-45, the worst mark on the floor. He did have three steals, and his first-quarter three off a Josh Giddey pass was one of Chicago’s four makes from deep all night.

 Giddey had six assists but went 1 of 10 for two points, and he picked up a technical foul early in the fourth quarter.
 Who Gave the Bulls Something
 Matas Buzelis led Chicago with 17 points, 13 from the line, and grabbed six rebounds. Jalen Smith scored the Bulls’ first eight points and finished with 15 points and eight rebounds in 19 minutes. Norman Powell added 15, and Tre Jones gave the second unit a lift with 13 points on 5-of-8 shooting off the bench.
 Kawhi Leonard , back in Toronto, scored 23 on 11-of-11 free throws. Barnes and Quickley also had 23 each, Quickley with seven assists, and RJ Barrett added 20.
 What’s On Tap Next
 Chicago was without Nic Claxton (hamstring), and Jordan Hawkins and Dailyn Swain both missed the game with an illness. The Bulls (0-1) visit Milwaukee on Friday, then open the United Center schedule against Washington on Saturday.
